tob-10481: Israel Abrahams wanders the side roads of Jewish literature in this charming collection of essays. He introduces medieval Hebrew poets, old prayer books, and forgotten storytellers, showing how Jews wrote and read across a thousand years of exile. The book is a guided stroll for anyone curious about the quieter corners of Jewish letters.
tob-4081: Al-Farabi — the ‘Second Master’ after Aristotle — wrote the Book of Letters on speech, logic, and God-lore. The great 900s Muslim thinker wed Greek thought to Islamic teaching. This work shows his way at its freshest. It is needful for students of medieval thought.
tob-4181: The Warner brothers’ Shahnama gives book one of Firdausi’s great Persian king-epic — Iran’s kings and champions from fable’s dawn to story. Their verse-Englishing bore the King-Book to our readers. Rustam’s and his peers’ tales are world classics. The high grandeur unfolds volume by volume.
tob-10781: Turner’s Arbatel — Of the Magic of the Ancients — is the 1655 English of the gentle 1575 grimoire. It teaches the magic of the Olympic spirits through prayer and purity of life. Its humane wisdom influenced later Rosicrucian thought. The work remains uniquely beloved among grimoires.
arxiv-2605-08881: When a user buys after seeing five ads, which ad deserves the credit? Yuguang Liu, Luyao Xia, Hu Liu, Zhangxi Yan, Jian Liang, and colleagues tackle multi-touch attribution with front-door causal methods, assigning credit across the creator ecosystem more honestly. The 2026 paper brings causal inference to advertising measurement.
arxiv-2605-09181: Tracking eyes through retinal images could diagnose disease — if the tracking survives real-world noise. Bo Wen, Dillon Lohr, Yatong An, and colleagues establish robust retinal eye tracking with a weakly supervised framework that needs little labeled data. The 2026 paper is medical computer vision built for the clinic.
arxiv-2605-09281: Mixture-of-experts models are huge, and quantizing their experts without wrecking them is delicate. Hongyaoxing Gu, Xinzhe Chen, Lijuan Hu, and Fangfang Liu propose TileQ: efficient low-rank quantization with 2D tiling. The 2026 paper shrinks giant mixture-of-experts models carefully.
arxiv-2605-09481: Time-sensitive networking — Ethernet with hard deadlines for factories and cars — is a specialized world. Rubi Debnath, Daniel Bujosa Mateu, Luxi Zhao, and colleagues benchmark how well LLMs handle it with TSNBench. The 2026 paper tests whether chatbots can do industrial networking.
arxiv-2605-09581: Event cameras see only changes — perfect for fast motion — and contrast maximization sharpens their noisy output. Michał Filipkowski, Marcin Kowalczyk, and Tomasz Kryjak build a dedicated FPGA hardware architecture for it. The 2026 paper is neuromorphic vision fully realized in silicon.
arxiv-2605-09681: Video diffusion models autoregress frame by frame, and the KV cache grows monstrous across long generations. Yicheng Ji, Zhizhou Zhong, Jun Zhang, and colleagues compress it hybrid-style with Forcing-KV. The 2026 paper makes autoregressive video generation leaner and faster.
arxiv-2605-09881: Jet-taggers classify particle jets at the LHC with neural networks; mechanistic interpretability dissects how they decide. This 2026 paper opens the black box of jet classification. It is particle physics meets interpretability at the high-energy frontier of modern physics today.
arxiv-2605-09981: Yeti tokenizes protein structures compactly — for reconstruction and multi-modal generation alike. Nabin Giri, Steven Farrell, Kristofer E. Bouchard, and colleagues build the compact tokenizer. The 2026 paper is protein AI with a compact vocabulary. It compresses the language of proteins.
arxiv-2605-10081: Microwave imaging in complex multipath environments needs polarization-aware ray-tracing enhanced back-projection. Han Na, Quanfeng Wang, and colleagues develop the algorithm. The 2026 paper is microwave imaging through clutter. It sees clearly through multipath interference, fully polarization-aware and precise.
pmc-13409081: Lupus autoimmune haemolytic anaemia — type I interferon targeted with anifrolumab, in the first report of its kind. Fulvia Ceccarelli, Rossella De Angelis, Francesca Bottazzi, and colleagues treat the patient. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is rheumatology. pmc-13544281: Anal cancer screening by artificial intelligence — a trinary model validated across centers and continents in high-resolution anoscopy. Miguel Martins, Miguel Mascarenhas, Joana Frias, and colleagues validate the AI. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is AI cancer screening. It teaches AI to spot anal precancer.
pmc-13454281: Dermatology targeted immunotherapies — their impact on autoimmune thyroid diseases, through cytokine-network crosstalk and thyroid safety. Jiahao Zhou, Ruiyang Han, and Tianshu Gao review the evidence. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is dermato-endocrinology. It warns skin drugs can stir the thyroid.
pmc-13437181: Children's dental injections — 4% buffered articaine versus 2% unbuffered lidocaine, in a double-blind randomized comparison. Ashish Suresh and Sunny Priyatham Tirupathi run the trial. arxiv-2606-17081: A. Ponce-Torres and colleagues peel graphite into graphene with a blast of transonic flow, air moving near the speed of sound. arxiv-2606-17281: Hyungwon Kim and colleagues check whether multimodal language models actually answer in the language they were spoken to. arxiv-2606-17581: Xiyu Zhai and colleagues present Visored, a controlled-natural-language prover for LLM-generated mathematics. The system checks AI-produced proofs written in readable language. It is a fact-checker for machine mathematics. It catches subtle proof errors that slip past casual reading.
arxiv-2606-18081: Vaibhav Tiwari adds a new rung to the chirp-mass ladder in gravitational-wave astronomy. The chirp mass encodes a binary's signature, and the new rung refines distance measurements. arxiv-2606-18181: Henry Bodwell and colleagues build IUU+DB, tracking illegal, unreported, and unregulated fishing alongside seafood fraud and labor abuses. arxiv-2606-18381: Amirhossein Abaskohi and colleagues search trees with attention guidance and progressive embeddings for long-document RAG in SproutRAG. plos-pone-0003381: Eye researchers traced a surprising villain in blindness in this 2008 immunology paper. plos-pone-0003481: HIV researchers found immune cells defending themselves in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003581: Cancer geneticists linked a kidney gene to cysts and tumors in this 2008 mouse study. The mouse model gives researchers a living system for a rare inherited cancer syndrome.
plos-pone-0003681: In 2008, Renesto, Rovery, and Schrenzel eavesdropped on a germ at the bite site. Rickettsia conorii, the tick-borne cause of Mediterranean spotted fever, was caught switching its genes on inside the skin sore. plos-pone-0003781: Martinovic, Gruber, and Müller asked how the brain binds features into objects in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003881: In 2008, a team argued fishing starves whole ecosystems, not just target fish. plos-pone-0003981: In 2008, Byakika-Tusiime, Chinn, and Oyugi tested generic HIV drugs against brand names. plos-pone-0004081: In 2009, Merad, Porumb, and Zargarian found a hidden grip in HIV's toolkit. An unusual helix-turn-helix motif in HIV-1 integrase bound viral DNA. The same motif also grabbed the host factor LEDGF. The double grip marks a target for blocking integration.
plos-pone-0004181: In 2009, Yang, Zhang, and Xu found a blood signal for a deadly fever. Serum platelet-activating factor acetylhydrolase activity marked severe leptospirosis cases. plos-pone-0004281: In 2009, Parker, Barkley, and Rino unmasked a TB wall-builder. The Rv3802c protein acted as a phospholipase/thioesterase in TB bacteria. An antimycobacterial compound blocked it. The enzyme's role spotlights a new drug target. The wall-building enzyme is key to TB's armor.
plos-pone-0004381: In 2009, Grenier, Teillet, and Grifone mapped the embryo face's builders. Neural crest cells and cranial mesoderm split head-muscle duties in embryos. plos-pone-0004481: In 2009, Middelbos, Vester, and Karr-Lilienthal read aging in dog muscle. Age and diet effects on gene expression in canine skeletal muscle were profiled. The beagles' muscles told diet and age stories. The data aid pet nutrition. The dogs were female beagles.
plos-pone-0004581: In 2009, Koliaraki, Marinou, and Vassilakopoulos built a handy blood-iron test. A novel immunological assay quantified hepcidin in human serum well. The iron-regulating peptide was finally measured. The neat tool aids anemia research today. The tiny peptide is small.
plos-pone-0004681: In 2009, Fatakia, Costanzi, and Chow hunted linked spots in smell-and-taste receptors. Highly correlated positions in GPCRs were computed via mutual information and graph theory. plos-pone-0004781: In 2009, Nowak and Barone found contrast adaptation steadying vision neurons anew. Contrast adaptation contributed to contrast-invariance of orientation tuning in primate V1. plos-pone-0345881: Why do gig workers keep driving, delivering, and freelancing when the pay is uncertain? This paper builds a typology — a map of types — of what motivates them, from the love of flexible hours to the need for cash. Sorting intrinsic and extrinsic drives, it gives platforms and policymakers a clearer picture of what actually keeps gig workers going.
plos-pone-0358781: Preeclampsia — dangerous high blood pressure in pregnancy — kills mothers in Kenya every year, and vitamin D deficiency is widespread. This matched case-control study compared vitamin D levels in Kenyan mothers who developed preeclampsia with those who did not. The results test whether a cheap supplement could become part of prevention.
plos-pone-0351281: Searching encrypted documents without decrypting them is a hard problem — harder still in Arabic, with its rich morphology. This paper evaluates preprocessing methods for dynamic searchable symmetric encryption of Arabic text. The empirical framework tells developers which text processing choices make encrypted Arabic search both fast and accurate.
plos-pone-0355381: A wild plant may protect the stomach from alcohol’s assault. This in vivo study showed Tragopogon coelesyriacus attenuates ethanol-induced gastric ulcers by calming oxidative stress, inflammation, and cell death. The plant emerges as a serious candidate for future ulcer-fighting drugs rooted in traditional knowledge.
plos-pone-0353681: Virus surveillance data has gaps — but epidemics don’t wait for complete records. This paper developed methods for estimating cumulative incidence from partially missing time series of respiratory viral infections. The math fills the gaps honestly, with uncertainty shown rather than hidden.
plos-pone-0358481: Stress ties the gut in knots — in pigs as in people. This paper tested surface electromyography as a non-invasive method for detecting stress-induced changes in gastrointestinal motility in pigs. The skin-surface readings offer researchers a painless, continuous window into the stressed gut.
plos-pone-0357381: Could electrical stimulation of muscles lift a depressed mind? This pilot randomized controlled trial protocol will test functional electrical stimulation for major depressive disorder. The planned trial explores an unconventional idea: whether zapping muscles can meaningfully improve mood.
plos-pone-0357181: In the ICU, immune status quietly shaped who survived the pandemic — and the gap widened late. This study found that outcomes of immunocompromised and non-immunocompromised patients diverged late in the pandemic. The late split reveals how the virus’s evolution changed the odds for the most vulnerable.
plos-pone-0356181: Exercise builds muscle — but the right recipe differs for rheumatic disease and age-related muscle loss. The Care for Muscle (C4M) study protocol will test the effects of exercise on muscle strength and characteristics in these groups. The planned trial tailors training to fragile muscles that can’t take standard programs.
plos-pone-0357581: Liquid bio-slurry can replace chemical nitrogen fertilizer for hot pepper farming. This Ethiopian study optimized nitrogen delivery via bio-slurry equivalent rations for hot pepper and soil productivity in the Amhara region. The organic approach boosts yields sustainably while cutting dependence on synthetic fertilizer.
plos-pone-0357281: Removing the superior cervical ganglion — a sympathetic nerve hub — worsened aortic dissection in mice. The finding implicates sympathetic nerves directly in aortic disease progression. The mouse model reveals a previously underappreciated mechanism that could reshape how scientists think about aortic catastrophe.
plos-pone-0355981: Microglia — the brain’s immune cells — respond to demyelination in complex, shifting ways. This paper mapped their multifaceted response in the cuprizone model of demyelination. The detailed portrait reveals microglia as dynamic players in myelin damage and repair, not mere bystanders.
plos-pone-0356781: A common lab protein — bovine serum albumin — can prime the mouse brain for a stronger reaction to bacterial toxins. This paper showed BSA sensitizes the mouse brain to lipopolysaccharides. The finding is a cautionary tale for neuroscientists: even ‘inert’ lab reagents can skew results.
plos-pone-0356381: Primary ocular-adnexal non-Hodgkin lymphoma — cancer around the eye — is rare and poorly documented in Latin America. This Peruvian cohort study reported an 18-year experience with the disease. The long-term data give regional oncologists the evidence base they’ve been missing.
plos-pone-0356281: Why do Pakistani women use — or avoid — contraception? This paper revisited the classic health belief model, adding fertility preferences and health system interaction as keys to contraceptive use. The enriched model explains decisions that simpler frameworks miss, pointing family planning programs toward what actually matters.
plos-pone-0356881: Some elementary schoolers simply refuse to go — and resilience may be the difference. This paper examined the associations of solution-building skills and resilience with school refusal behavior among elementary students. The findings point schools toward building children’s coping capacity rather than merely punishing absence.
plos-pone-0356481: Immigrants’ health in England and Wales varies dramatically by country of birth — but detailed data were missing. This total-population, repeated cross-sectional study measured immigrant life expectancy and disability-free life expectancy by detailed birth country. The granular findings reveal which migrant groups thrive and which suffer — essential for equitable health policy.
plos-pone-0355481: When mothers work, do Nepali children eat better or worse? This paper examined the impact of maternal employment on child health and nutrition with evidence from Nepal. The findings untangle income gains from time losses — informing policies that support working mothers without shortchanging children.
plos-pone-0355781: Biochar enhanced with rock minerals holds a hydrogen puzzle. This paper investigated pyrogenic coatings, mineral redox chemistry, and pore accessibility in rock-enhanced biochar. Solving the puzzle unlocks biochar’s full potential for carbon sequestration and soil restoration.
plos-pone-0354981: Glioblastoma might be attacked with repurposed Alzheimer’s and ovarian cancer drugs — activated by ultrasound. This paper used positive-unlabeled learning plus 3D bioprinting to repurpose drugs as sonosensitizers for glioblastoma. The AI-guided repurposing could fast-track new weapons against the deadliest brain cancer.
plos-pone-0355681: Yeast cells tune gene expression to glucose availability through layered regulation. This paper uncovered dual regulatory mechanisms controlling YGP1 expression in Saccharomyces cerevisiae in response to glucose. The findings illuminate the sophisticated nutrient sensing of biology’s favorite model organism.
plos-pone-0355181: Sudden sensorineural hearing loss — waking up deaf in one ear — may involve homocysteine. This prospective clinical study found evidence for hyperhomocysteinemia in these patients. The findings suggest a blood marker — and possibly a treatable metabolic contributor — for a frightening condition.
plos-pone-0343481: Food preferences — and gender — shape how the prefrontal cortex responds while eating. This exploratory study used functional near-infrared spectroscopy to map those responses in medial and frontopolar regions. The findings reveal the neural choreography of liking — and how it differs between men and women.
plos-pone-0347081: Meta-analysts waste hours transcribing data from bar charts in published papers. This paper built a computer vision approach for automatically extracting data from bar chart raster images. The automated extraction accelerates evidence synthesis across biomedicine — turning pictures back into numbers.
plos-pone-0355281: COPD exacerbations — sudden, dangerous worsenings — may involve neutrophils wearing PD-L1. This paper examined neutrophil PD-L1 expression’s role in acute exacerbation. The findings suggest the immune checkpoint better known from cancer also governs lung crises — a potential therapeutic crossover.
plos-pone-0354681: Childhood anemia — might prebiotics, probiotics, or synbiotics help? This systematic review and meta-analysis examined their efficacy and safety on hemoglobin and anemia in children. The pooled evidence tests whether gut microbes can be harnessed against one of childhood’s commonest afflictions.
plos-pone-0352681: Coal fractures — temporarily plugged with particles — behave in simulatable ways. This numerical study examined pressure response and fluid loss mechanisms. The findings optimize the fracturing that unlocks coalbed methane — energy with engineering precision.
plos-pone-0332781: Sludge-water interfaces — in treatment tanks — need precise measurement. This paper measured them via adjustable ultrasonic echo energy peak points. The acoustic method pinpoints the murky boundary where solids settle. The findings improve wastewater treatment control — cleaner effluent through better sensing.
plos-pone-0353381: Trauma triage decisions — physicians’ — measured by technology-enhanced simulation. This paper developed and evaluated that simulation. The virtual patients tested real decision-making under pressure. The findings reveal how doctors actually triage — toward training that saves the right lives.
plos-pone-0353781: Dyslexia screening for secondary students — its face validity — examined. This paper did so. The validity check asked whether the instrument looks right to those who’ll use it. The findings are the first gate — before psychometric rigor — toward identifying struggling teen readers.
plos-pone-0354181: Fracture healing in mice — sequentially treated with sclerostin antibody then parathyroid hormone. This tibial osteotomy study showed differential modulation. The findings revealed order matters — bone-building drugs sequenced for synergy. The research informs the pharmacology of mending broken bones.
plos-pone-0352981: Acrocomia palms — flowering seasonality synchronized by photoperiod. This paper shed light on it. The findings revealed day length orchestrating tropical palm reproduction. The research served both ecology and agriculture — flowering predicted, harvests planned.
plos-pone-0353881: Prosthetic socket liner strain — measured by digital image correlation versus finite element analysis. This preliminary comparison did so. The findings validated computational models against physical measurement. The research improved prosthetic comfort — liners designed by verified simulation.
plos-pone-0353481: Public soybean breeding programs — implementing genomic selection with limited budgets. This paper laid out strategies for doing so. The approaches balanced genotyping costs against genetic gain. The findings brought cutting-edge breeding to public institutions — better soybeans for farmers who can’t afford private-sector seed prices.
plos-pone-0352881: Peruvian tuberculosis — first- and second-line drug-resistant isolates under genetic surveillance. This paper did so. The findings mapped resistance mutations nationally. The research guided the treatment — the right regimen for each resistant strain. The national scope is the strength: it captures resistance patterns across Peru’s diverse regions, not just Lima’s hospitals.
plos-pone-0353181: Autism and irritable bowel — shared molecular signature in dysregulated glucocorticoid-responsive immune genes. This paper identified it in peripheral blood cells. The findings linked stress hormones, immunity, and autism. The research bridged the brain-gut divide — one signature, two conditions.
plos-pone-0352781: Blockchain in government operations — adoption enhanced through a comprehensive user framework. This paper built it. The findings mapped the bureaucratic path to the chain. The research served the digitization — the state, distributed. The user-adoption focus is the realism: governments fail at technology when they ignore the humans who must use it.
plos-pone-0352581: Bioactive cellulose acetate electrospun films — data-driven classification and design for active food packaging. This paper did so. The analysis engineered the film’s antimicrobial action. Its food science value is freshness. The work spins the packaging that protects. The data-driven design is the acceleration: it predicts the best film formulations instead of testing them all.
plos-pone-0350181: Washington’s killer whales — Bigg’s increasing presence and Southern Residents’ changing seasonality. This paper documented both. The analysis contrasted the mammal-eaters’ rise with the fish-eaters’ shifting calendar. The finding signals an ecological changing of the guard. The work watches the orcas’ Salish Sea reshuffle.
plos-pone-0351081: Pediatric pneumonia detection — interpretable machine learning via symbolic classification of radiomic texture and morphology from chest X-rays. This paper built it. The analysis made the AI’s reasoning readable. The finding diagnoses transparently. The work reads the child’s chest, symbolically.
plos-pone-0351881: Post-2022 monkeypox strains — a multi-epitope vaccine designed via pan-genome and reverse vaccinology. This paper did so. The analysis computed the vaccine from the genomes. The finding is the blueprint. The work designs the mpox shot in silico. The post-2022 strains are the target: the vaccine is designed for the currently circulating viruses, not historical ones.
europmc-pmc2850381: Before a cell divides, its nucleus and centrosome must move into position. This 2010 paper shows the motor proteins dynein and kinesin-1, linked by Bicaudal D2, associate with nuclear pores to regulate that positioning during mitotic entry. The authors map the machinery. Their work reveals the logistics behind cell division.
europmc-pmc2870981: A century-old chemical reaction keeps finding new tricks. This 2010 review tours new developments in the Friedel-Crafts alkylation, from green chemistry to asymmetric catalysis. The authors show an old workhorse renewed. Their tour connects classic organic chemistry to modern clean methods.
europmc-pmc2872881: Pea aphids live with many microbes yet rarely get sick, and this 2010 paper asks why. The authors survey immunity and other defenses in the pea aphid Acyrthosiphon pisum. Their overview reveals unusual immune gaps. The work explains how a major crop pest tolerates its germ load.
europmc-pmc2885081: Chitin and chitosan, from shells and fungi, need careful characterization before use. This 2010 review surveys spectroscopic methods for their structural analysis. The authors compare the tools of the trade, from infrared to NMR. Their guide helps labs verify exactly what material they have.
europmc-pmc2888581: Mothers and children die in huge numbers across Sub-Saharan Africa, and this 2010 paper asks where and why. The authors map the deaths and their causes. Their analysis points to preventable gaps in care. The paper became a blueprint for saving lives in the region.
europmc-pmc2896381: Seeing biology in 3D takes the right tools. This 2010 paper presents a high-level 3D visualization API for Java and ImageJ, the beloved microscope software. The authors' interface lets biologists render volumes with little code. Their tool brought 3D views to everyday lab microscopes everywhere.
europmc-pmc2908081: HPV's role in throat cancers needed quantifying, and this 2010 meta-analysis delivers. The authors weigh HPV's impact on cancer risk and survival in head and neck squamous cell carcinomas. Their pooling clarifies the virus's toll. The work refined prognosis and vaccine arguments.
europmc-pmc2939781: Bile duct cancers are rare and brutal, and this 2010 Japanese study compares treatments. The authors test gemcitabine alone versus paired with cisplatin in biliary tract cancer. Their multicenter data favors the combo. The result shaped care guidelines in Asia. Oncologists still follow its lead.
europmc-pmc3002981: Stressed cells reprogram their tRNA decorations. This 2010 paper shows cells retune tRNA chemical marks when stress hits. The authors uncover the retuning with systems math. Their work links tRNA to stress defense. The marks act like dimmer switches on genes.
europmc-pmc3061881: Wiping mouse gut germs reshapes the gut. This 2011 paper shows antibiotics that clear mouse gut germs remake the gut lining. The authors reveal the reshaping. Their work informs germ science. The lining thins without its germs. Repopulating germs reverses the damage.
europmc-pmc3113981: Non-inferiority trials got a plain guide. This 2011 paper explains non-inferiority trial design through the looking glass. The authors clarify the logic. Their guide aids trialists. New drugs need only match old ones. The margins must be set with care.
europmc-pmc3166781: Bone disorders got reclassified. This 2011 paper revises how genetic bone disorders are grouped. The authors sort hundreds of conditions. Their work guides gene doctors. europmc-pmc3168881: A T-cell marker got identified. This 2011 paper shows Helios expression marks T cell activation and proliferation. The authors reveal the marker. Their work aids immunology. europmc-pmc3222181: Phones got drafted against depression. This 2011 paper prototypes a phone app for depression that reads the user's context. The authors prove the concept. Their work launched mobile mental health. Location and activity fed the app. The concept seeded a research wave.
europmc-pmc3257681: Nuts got a health review. This 2010 paper surveys the health benefits of eating nuts. The author grades the evidence. Their overview guides diets. Walnuts led the heart benefits. A handful a day sufficed. Ros's review is widely cited. The review shaped dietary advice.
europmc-pmc3266881: Ancestry maps got a haplotype method. This 2012 paper infers population structure from dense haplotype data. The authors' method sharpens the maps. Their work spread through labs. fineSTRUCTURE grew from the method. The tool is open source. Lawson's team led the work.
europmc-pmc3399081: Ultra-long insulin got a design paper. This 2012 paper designs how insulin degludec lasts over a day. The authors reveal the mechanism. Their work guides diabetes care. Jonassen's team led the work. The drug reached patients. The paper is widely cited.
europmc-pmc3400581: Telomere lengthening got a hallmark. This 2012 paper shows ATRX gene loss marks the ALT telomere pathway. The authors reveal the hallmarks. Their work guides cancer research. Lovejoy's team led the work. The paper is a landmark. It is widely cited.
europmc-pmc3460881: Plant control genes got validated. This 2012 paper validates control genes for virus-infected tobacco studies. The authors reveal the validation. Their work guides labs. Liu's team led the work. The paper is widely cited. Labs use the genes. The study is a classic.
europmc-pmc6536981: Pancreatic cancer that cannot be surgically removed leaves few options - but MRI-guided radiation can aim higher doses precisely at the tumor while sparing nearby organs. This study reports outcomes for inoperable patients treated with adaptive MR-guided radiotherapy, including dose-escalated cases. europmc-pmc6549181: One small SARS protein - ORF-8b - punches above its weight: it stresses infected cells and trips the NLRP3 inflammasome, a molecular fire alarm. europmc-pmc6600381: A severed spinal cord triggers a destructive chain reaction - the secondary injury - that kills more nerve cells than the initial blow. europmc-pmc6642581: Severe flu kills not just through the virus but through the body's own firestorm. europmc-pmc6700281: Which protein-coding DNA changes raise diabetes risk? europmc-pmc6722781: Neutrophils - first-responder immune cells - can explode, casting webs of DNA studded with antimicrobials. europmc-pmc6737581: Drug-resistant germs are outrunning old surveillance - but DNA sequencing can track them. europmc-pmc6830681: Aging is not just years - it is what the body can still do. This long-term study tested the WHO's 'intrinsic capacity' concept: whether a single score tracks aging's many domains and flags decline. The measure could reshape elder care. One number for how well we age.
europmc-pmc6864381: Racism is not just wrong - it makes people sick. This review maps studies tying self-reported racial discrimination to health state and care use. The evidence ties discrimination to worse health ills. Fairness is a health medicine. The results call for action outside the clinic.
europmc-pmc6927181: Single cell counts need evening out - this is the gold standard. This paper offers leveling and spread steadying of single cell RNA-seq data using tuned minus two-outcome fit. The recipe behind Seurat SCTransform. Lab noise, by math gone. The recipe splits life signals from lab runs.
gao-gaoreports-b-310081: One of GAO's biggest consolidated bid-protest rulings of 2007, joining nine docket numbers filed by timber companies — Poston Logging, Shasta Green, Sierra Cedar, Trinity River, and others. gao-gaoreports-b-299981: A 2007 GAO ruling on two linked contract fights from Navarro Research and Engineering, Inc. gao-gaoreports-gao-07-281: Spare parts were taking too long to buy in 2007, and GAO's report says the Pentagon could better manage its acquisition lead times. The findings target the delays. The report's logic: the war machine should not wait on its own supply chain.

openalex-w7206213381: Some texts repeat the same words over and over; others use varied vocabulary. This computational linguistics paper proposes a simple way to sort documents into high and low lexical repetition using Yule's K, a classic measure of vocabulary concentration, paired with k-means clustering. The authors test the method with Monte Carlo simulation. A neat, technical contribution to the toolkit for automatically characterizing writing style.
arxiv-2606-16081: A pure math paper about the playbook of shape-math: how big math frames act on spaces. It builds 'cut and paste' moves for neat gangs of math things (simple-minded systems) inside mirror-like frames. The fine print is for algebra pros only.
arxiv-2606-16181: Altermagnets are a fresh-found class of magnet stuff with odd traits that may drive next-gen gear. This paper eyes the gem-cut of Ca3(Ru,Ti)2O7, a hoped-for 'polar' case, to test if its build truly earns the name. It is rock-physics for magnet-tech hunters.
arxiv-2606-16281: Masked diffusion language models generate text by filling in blanks, and ensembling several of them can improve quality — but which model should lead at each step? This paper tracks reliable generation trajectories to decide who leads decoding when. It targets AI researchers improving diffusion-based alternatives to standard autoregressive models.
arxiv-2606-16781: Quantum chromodynamics (QCD) describes quarks and gluons — the building blocks of matter. Sharper math, truer quarks.
arxiv-2606-16881: Robot teams mapping together must merge their maps — distributed SLAM. SGM-SLAM matches scene graphs (maps of objects and relations) to do it with less data. It is for robotics researchers building multi-robot mapping. Many bots, one map. Graphs beat raw points.
